meta.description: Pool of verified, public-domain chess quotes (English) by famous players. One quote per UTC day is rendered into the About page (README.md) between the daily-quote markers by scripts/update-quote.py (run by .github/workflows/daily-quote.yml). The pool itself is intentionally not linked from the navigation - only the rendered daily quote is visible.
meta.rotation: index = floor(unix_ms_utc / 86400000) % quotes.length  (same deterministic UTC-day rule as the daily puzzles in data/puzzles/)
meta.license: Every author in this pool died in 1955 or earlier, so their works are in the public domain in the EU (life + 70 years) as of 2026; several works were also published <= 1929 and are public domain in the US. See licenses/quotes-public-domain.md for the full reasoning, the verification log and the exclusion list.
meta.verification: Each quote was checked on 2026-11-23 (UTC) against at least two independent sources (listed in 'sources'), preferring primary texts (books/periodicals, several hosted PD in data/books/) and Edward Winter's sourced Chess Notes (chesshistory.com). Misattributed or unsourced famous lines were rejected - see licenses/quotes-public-domain.md.
meta.authorsPolicy: Only players with no documented negative headlines are quoted. Players deliberately excluded (documented controversies): Bobby Fischer, Alexander Alekhine, Efim Bogoljubow; also excluded for copyright reasons (died after 1955): Savielly Tartakower, Frank Marshall, Akiba Rubinstein, etc.

quotes.quote: Pawns are the soul of chess.
quotes.author: François-André Danican Philidor
quotes.original: « ... les Pions. Ils sont l'âme des Echecs. »
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1795; work published 1749 -> public domain worldwide.
quotes.notes: First printing traced by Edward Winter to L'Analyze des Echecs (London, 1749), p. xix; the customary English rendering is 'Pawns are the soul of chess'.

quotes.quote: Only the player with the initiative has the right to attack.
quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1900; works published <= 1891 -> public domain worldwide.
quotes.notes: Core Steinitz principle (Hooper, 'Steinitz' Theory', British Chess Magazine 1984); widely documented.

quotes.quote: A win by an unsound combination, however showy, fills me with artistic horror.
quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1900; periodical published <= 1891 -> public domain worldwide.
quotes.notes: Documented in Steinitz's own periodical; quoted in Winter's Steinitz pages.

quotes.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
quotes.work: Letter to H. M. Gorham and W. E. Lester, 13 April 1888 (in The Steinitz Papers, Landsberger 2002, pp. 95-96)
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1900; letter published 1888/2002 edition of PD-era papers -> public domain.
quotes.notes: Winter traces 'mental gymnastics' to Steinitz's own 1888 letter ('our mental gymnastics offered more relief to a philosophical mind...'). Distinct from Pascal's earlier 'gymnase de l'esprit'.

quotes.quote: Chess is neither a science nor an art. It is what human nature most delights in — a fight.
quotes.author: Emanuel Lasker
quotes.work: Common Sense in Chess (1919), p. 9; also Lasker's Manual of Chess (1925), p. 9
quotes.original: By some ardent enthusiasts Chess has been elevated into a science or an art. It is neither; but its principal characteristic seems to be — what human nature mostly delights in — a fight.
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1941 (EU: PD since 2012); works published 1919/1925 (US: PD pre-1930). Hosted PD copy: data/books/en/lasker-s-manual-of-chess.txt.
quotes.notes: Shortened to the two closing sentences of the documented passage.

quotes.quote: On the chessboard, lies and hypocrisy do not survive long.
quotes.author: Emanuel Lasker
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1941; work published 1925 -> public domain (EU since 2012, US pre-1930). Hosted PD copy: data/books/en/lasker-s-manual-of-chess.txt.
quotes.notes: Verbatim in the hosted 1925 Manual text ('On the chessboard lies and hypocrisy do not survive long.').

quotes.quote: I keep on fighting as long as my opponent can make a mistake.
quotes.author: Emanuel Lasker
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1941; work published 1925 -> public domain. Hosted PD copy: data/books/en/lasker-s-manual-of-chess.txt.
quotes.notes: Widely cited to the Manual of Chess; chess-internal dispute about the 1910 Schlechter match is not a scandal - Lasker himself was persecuted as a Jew and fled Nazi Germany in 1933.

quotes.quote: In order to improve your game, you must study the endgame before anything else.
quotes.author: José Raúl Capablanca
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1942 (EU: PD since 2013); work published 1921 (US: PD pre-1930). Hosted PD copy: data/books/en/chessfundamental00capa.txt.
quotes.notes: Opening sentence of the documented passage; the full sentence continues '...for whereas the endings can be studied and mastered by themselves, the middlegame and the opening must be studied in relation to the endgame.'

quotes.quote: You may learn much more from a game you lose than from a game you win.
quotes.author: José Raúl Capablanca
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1942 -> public domain in the EU since 2013; short quote, fully attributed.
quotes.notes: Often paired with 'You will have to lose hundreds of games before becoming a good player.' (same source); first sentence quoted alone here. NOT the unsourced 'I see only one move ahead, but it is always the correct one' (Winter: no known source).

quotes.quote: In chess, as played by a good player, logic and imagination must go hand in hand, compensating each other.
quotes.author: José Raúl Capablanca
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1942; work published 1921 -> public domain (EU + US). Hosted PD copy: data/books/en/chessfundamental00capa.txt.

quotes.quote: Chess, like love, like music, has the power to make men happy.
quotes.author: Siegbert Tarrasch
quotes.work: Das Schachspiel (Berlin, 1931), p. 4; English: The Game of Chess (London, 1935), p. xi
quotes.original: Das Schach hat wie die Liebe, wie die Musik die Fähigkeit, den Menschen glücklich zu machen.
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1934 -> public domain in the EU since 2005.
quotes.notes: Primary source page given verbatim by Edward Winter. Tarrasch (Jewish-born, converted 1909) was himself a target of Nazi-era antisemitism - no negative headlines of his own.

quotes.quote: Before the endgame, the gods have placed the middlegame.
quotes.author: Siegbert Tarrasch
quotes.work: Das Schachspiel (Berlin, 1931), p. 306; The Game of Chess (London, 1935), p. 217
quotes.original: Aber vor das Endspiel haben die Götter das Mittelspiel gesetzt.
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1934 -> public domain in the EU since 2005.
quotes.notes: Winter documents two occurrences of the German original in Tarrasch's own writings.

quotes.quote: The threat is stronger than the execution.
quotes.author: Aron Nimzowitsch
quotes.work: My System (1925); anecdote via Brinckmann, Deutsche Schachblätter 1932 / BCM July 1932, p. 307
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1935 (EU: PD since 2006); My System published 1925 (US: PD pre-1930). Hosted PD copy: data/books/en/nimzowitsch-my-system.txt.
quotes.notes: Customary attribution to Nimzowitsch (Winter notes the principle was formulated earlier by K. Eisenbach, 1908, and once ascribed to Tartakower - but Nimzowitsch is the standard, documented attribution tied to My System).

quotes.quote: There is more real chess truth in ideas than in variations.
quotes.author: Richard Réti
quotes.work: Masters of the Chessboard (New York, 1932; German orig. 1933)
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1929 -> public domain in the EU since 2000.
quotes.notes: Verbatim in the book's opening chapter ('There is more real chess truth in ideas than in variations.').

quotes.quote: Play the opening like a book, the middlegame like a magician, and the endgame like a machine.
quotes.author: Rudolf Spielmann
quotes.work: Chess Rules of Thumb (Chernev), p. 103, as quoted by Spielmann; also quoted by Winter
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1942 -> public domain in the EU since 2013.
quotes.notes: Winter attributes the line to Spielmann ('The Austrian Rudolf Spielmann wrote that we must...'); he also flags that Chernev's book layout is ambiguous - hence the extra independent attributions.

quotes.quote: It is generally the shortcoming of a young player that he does not keep abreast of the theory of the game.
quotes.author: Géza Maróczy
quotes.work: American Chess Bulletin, October 1906, p. 212 (also May 1906, p. 85)
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1951 (EU: PD since 2022); periodical published 1906 (US: PD pre-1930).
quotes.notes: Two independent citations of the 1906 American Chess Bulletin. Maróczy: clean record (Capablanca called him 'very gentlemanly and correct').

quotes.quote: Let the chessboard supersede the card table, and a great improvement will be visible in the morals of the community.
quotes.author: Paul Morphy
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1884; work published 1859 -> public domain worldwide.
quotes.notes: Original spelling 'supercede' normalized to 'supersede'. NOT used: the apocryphal 'The ability to play chess well is the sign of a wasted life' (Skeptics StackExchange: no evidence Morphy said it).

quotes.quote: To win a tournament, a competitor must in the first place play well, but he should also have a good amount of luck.
quotes.author: Adolf Anderssen
quotes.work: As told to Steinitz; International Chess Magazine, August 1886, p. 236
quotes.pdBasis: Author died 1879; periodical published 1886 -> public domain worldwide.
quotes.notes: Steinitz quoting Anderssen verbatim in his own magazine; traced by Winter in three Chess Notes items.
